pages.name: Time-Tracking
pages.html:
Time-Tracking: Time is the most vital resource in the world of Spacer, since all activities take time to complete. When employed to complete a job within a time frame, there is a further financial incentive to manage time. Accomplishing different tasks will use up time. The Activity Time table can be used to aid referees to help determine time frames.

Example of Weekly Time Usage, including for Travelling:

  • Week 1) Pay the loan and crew, then find work in a starport; load the ship and travel into space to reach the jump point
  • Week 2) Enter jump-space and spend one week travelling, then exit jump-space.
  • Week 3) Travel to the next starport; u goods and find a new job, then return to space.
  • Week 4) Enter jump-space to head towards the next objective, then exit jumpspace after a week.
  • Start back at Week 1 and repeat.

Book p.15

pages.name: Activity Time
pages.html:
Activity Time: All activities done by spacers take time to resolve. Use the following table to help inform how much time is needed to do a task. Attempting to complete an activity faster represents decreasing the amount of required time by one step but may incur a negative DM or gain a positive DM per the referee’s discretion.

Interval of TimeExamples
10 Seconds
  • Combat round, pg. 40
10 Minutes
  • Performing a non-combat Skill, pg. 28
  • Space combat round beyond dogfighting range, pg. 84
  • Exploring and searching a room or ship corridor
  • Putting on a vaccsuit
1 Hour
  • Fully searching a cargo container
  • Repair 1 hull point of damage of a starship
6 Hours
  • Gathering information and rumours, pg. 56
  • Travelling over land, pg.98
  • Taking inventory of a ship’s cargo
  • Building shelter
  • Repairing a hit to a vehicle
1 Day
  • Repair damage to a ship system in a starport
1D Days
  • Tracking down a job, pg. 50

Book p.15
